_note: The record of hand-authored fragment edits, replayed idempotently by apply_retrofit.py (build.py step 1). Ops: strip_span / text / untag_word / retag_word (whole-unit), unwrap / retag / add (per-verse) -- see apply_retrofit.py. Once units exist, the committed units/*.html will already contain all of this; these entries are the audit trail and the safety net for port_artifact.py, which re-runs fragment extraction on a unit it (re)ports. Unit 1's entries: the artifact already wrapped every tracked-root occurrence in a span, so this is all data-w injection (retag, from==to), not new tagging -- except the v15 'rest' pair, where the artifact rendered one Hebrew word (yaniaḥ) as two English words ('gives ... rest') in two separate spans; only 'rest' is tagged (data-w, class r) since it's the word a reader actually recognizes as the root -- 'gives' is left plain, untagged (2026-09-17, Lane: a class='rl' echo on 'gives' still picked up the root's colour/underline via the generic [data-root] CSS selector, which read as 'gives is part of the rest thread' and was more confusing than helpful, especially since 'gives' is also the plain word for the separate give/natan thread elsewhere in the unit -- a lighter-weight tag on a second word for one Hebrew occurrence isn't actually lighter to a reader). The `unwrap` entry below exists purely to keep this idempotent against any earlier state that had 'gives' tagged. 'occ' (added to retag alongside this unit) picks the Nth same-root-same-text span in a verse, needed where one root renders the same English word twice in a verse (v11, v15 'possess').
